review:
Blockwick 2 is a thoughtfully designed and surprisingly deep puzzle game that takes a familiar concept and expands it into something far richer and more rewarding than it initially appears. Developed and published by Kieffer Bros., the game builds upon classic sliding-block logic while layering in originality, elegance, and a remarkable amount of handcrafted content. At a glance, its bright colors and simple grids suggest a casual experience, but beneath that inviting surface lies a puzzle game that consistently challenges spatial reasoning, long-term planning, and creative problem-solving.

The core objective in Blockwick 2 is deceptively simple: slide blocks around a grid until all blocks of the same color are touching one another. There are no timers, no move limits, and no pressure to perform quickly, which immediately establishes a relaxed and contemplative pace. Early puzzles ease players into this concept with small boards and clear solutions, allowing the rules to feel intuitive and approachable. However, as the game progresses, the puzzles steadily grow more intricate, demanding not only an understanding of block positioning but also foresight about how each move will cascade through the entire board.

What truly distinguishes Blockwick 2 is the sheer variety of mechanics introduced over time. The game continually expands its puzzle language with new block types and behaviors that radically alter how problems must be approached. Some blocks are linked together, causing multiple pieces to move simultaneously, while others behave like segmented creatures that must be maneuvered as a single entity. Sticky blocks cling together unexpectedly, immovable blocks force players to work around fixed constraints, and layered interactions often require several preparatory moves before a meaningful shift can occur. These mechanics never feel gimmicky; instead, they are carefully integrated so that each new concept builds naturally on the last.

The game’s structure also adds depth beyond simple completion. Many levels contain optional objectives that encourage more thoughtful play, such as uncovering hidden moon pearls or achieving special “illumination” solutions by covering specific symbols on the board. These optional challenges do not block progression, but they offer an additional layer of satisfaction for players who enjoy perfecting solutions rather than merely finding any solution. This design choice respects different play styles, allowing casual players to move forward while giving dedicated puzzle enthusiasts meaningful goals to pursue.

Content volume is another major strength. Blockwick 2 offers an extensive collection of puzzles, including a large main campaign and an additional set of foundational puzzles that reinforce core mechanics. With hundreds of carefully crafted levels, the game provides dozens of hours of gameplay for those determined to see everything it has to offer. Importantly, this length never feels padded or repetitive, as later puzzles often remix earlier mechanics in unexpected ways, forcing players to rethink assumptions and adapt their strategies.

Visually and audibly, the game supports its puzzle focus with a clean and calming presentation. The colorful, minimalist art style makes it easy to read the board at a glance, while subtle animations provide clear feedback for each move. The soundtrack and ambient sound design are gentle and unobtrusive, contributing to a meditative atmosphere that encourages concentration rather than tension. Controls are smooth and precise, ensuring that any difficulty comes from the puzzle itself rather than awkward input or interface friction.

While the difficulty curve is generally well paced, there are moments where challenge spikes noticeably, particularly when multiple mechanics intersect in a single puzzle. The game offers minimal direct instruction for new block behaviors, relying instead on experimentation and discovery. For some players, this can lead to brief moments of confusion, but for others it enhances the sense of accomplishment when a solution finally clicks. These moments reinforce the game’s identity as one that trusts the player’s intelligence and patience.

Ultimately, Blockwick 2 stands as an excellent example of how a simple idea can be elevated through careful design, creativity, and respect for the player. It does not rely on spectacle or narrative hooks, instead delivering satisfaction through pure logical engagement and steady mastery of its systems. For fans of thoughtful puzzle games who enjoy taking their time, exploring layered mechanics, and savoring well-earned solutions, Blockwick 2 offers a rich, polished, and deeply rewarding experience that easily earns its place among standout indie puzzle titles.

A very relaxing, zen puzzle game. Low-stress gameplay, calming music, pleasant design aesthetic, satisfying sound design. The puzzles usually feature obvious sub-goals that lead to a steady flow of moments where you feel like you've made progress.

Throughout the game the puzzles feel very well designed. Each chapter introduces a single new mechanic, and while the mechanics are simple they lead to some complex puzzles. Some of the puzzles are quite hard, but every level has an easy sub-objective that allows you to skip it (effectively this just forces you to engage with the level briefly before you can skip). And if you want more challenge, each level has a bonus objective of covering all the symbols with color blocks (although this is only fun on some levels, and you need to fiddle around with the white/gray blocks just to see the symbols).

One gripe: For a game that's more focused on aesthetic than on gameplay, it feels fair to criticize accessibility. Some of the block colors are a bit too close together, especially since the sleep effect changes a block's shade slightly. More glaringly, when white blocks are linked together it is impossible to see the symbols on them (at least on my monitor), so you can only tell which ones are linked by guessing or by trial and error. This problem ironically goes away when the colors darken after you beat the level. There are no options to mitigate either of these problems.

Overall, if you're looking for a fancy, innovative, exciting puzzle game, this isn't it. But if you're looking at something relaxing that can both hold 100% of your attention and keep you busy while watching TV, or just something really calming, this is a good choice.

If you're a serious puzzle gamer, and even if you're just looking for something to kill a few minutes here and there, Blockwick 2 is a good time. The main goal of the game is to match all the blocks of the same color (except for the white "garbage" ones) in a given area. You do this by sliding them around, much like those old sliding-block toys where the goal is to create a picture, except this time both the playfields and the pieces come in many more shapes than just squares.

There are other gimmicks as well: "sleeping" blocks, blocks that can only move as part of a set, block chains (heh), and so on. The sticky and multicolored tumbling blocks are the most frustrating ones to deal with, but they are manageable enough, and not so bad that they made me want to give up on the game.

In general, the puzzles are very well designed, and each one has two secondary goals for completionists. One of these, the hidden pearls, is also useful for when you need to skip a puzzle that's too hard. However, veteran puzzle fans should have little trouble completing the main goals, and the other bonus goal, that involves matching blocks over runes, provides a good bit of challenge.

If I have one complaint (besides certain sometimes annoying special blocks), it's that the difficulty between puzzles is a little uneven, particularly in the "Basics" sets. Otherwise, I found this game to be just what I needed at the time I picked it up. if you're in the mood for a good, low-key puzzle game, I recommend you do the same.

[i]Blockwick 2[/i] is an advanced spin on the classic puzzle of moving blocks around a grid to unscramble a picture or pattern sequence. However in B2 you only have to arrange same-color blocks so that they all connect. And while that may sound pretty easy -- and is at Level 1-- it gets a lot more tricky when new kinds of blocks are introduced:

[list]
[*]blocks required for the solution but are fixed in place
[*]blocks that don't touch but move in tandem
[*]blocks that form chains and move like a caterpillar
[*]rolling blocks whose color is what is currently face up
[*]blocks that are only movable after the same color touches them
[*]blocks that immobilize colored blocks if they touch
[*]sticky blocks that attach to others and have to be peeled off using other surfaces
[/list]

Combine a bunch of these and you can have a formidable challenge in front of you. Not to mention some puzzles are so tightly packed or have blocks with such odd shapes that getting enough space to move larger ones seems almost impossible. There's also a bonus win scenario called "illumination" where the color blocks are arranged properly but also cover three glyphs on the puzzle. This usually involves quite a bit more experimentation to position the blocks correctly. 

I did most of these on my own, but there were many where I had to go to a guide because I didn't want to spend hours trying to figure them out. The game can be a little frustrating in that regard, but there's also a means of skipping a puzzle if it's too hard so you can come back to it later. The interface is smooth and intuitive -- really it's just click-hold a block and drag it around.

If you like puzzle games I highly recommend this, although it will take a LONG time to finish if you are a completionist. The main game has 10 levels and 160 puzzles, but there is also a "Basics" section that adds 144 more, albeit less challenging puzzles that were a part of the first Blockwick game. I didn't bother finishing them because after 27 hours I had my fill! However the full retail price on Steam gets you more than your money's worth.

Blockwick 2 is a game about moving blocks around until all blocks of the same color make contact with each other. Sounds easy but I assure you it's much more complicated than that. Some of the blocks are bolted down and can’t move while others are forced to move when moving a different block. This type of puzzle is not the kind that you end up getting frustrated at when you can’t solve it since the game lets you progress to the next level if you can find the hidden pear in every level. The soundtrack is very nice and goes with the game very well and can even be purchased on Bandcamp if you wish.

Blockwick 2 is a puzzle game with simple but aesthetically pleasing visuals where you move around various blocks to try to connect blocks that are alike in color. There are various worlds/chapters/sections, with new types of blocks introduced every so often to make the puzzles more difficult to solve.

I found, overall, that this is a challenging but entertaining puzzle game! I really enjoyed the concept and the new mechanics as they were introduced. The goals and instructions are straightforward, making it easy to see what you can do and how you can do it, but harder to actually get the blocks to the solution right away. This forces you to really think spatially to find the solution. 

I personally found that the difficulty wasn't too high. It didn't gradually increase and instead I found myself going through most of the puzzles with relative ease with one random puzzle every once in a while that would spike in difficulty, leaving me struggling to find the solution for a good long while (note that I was going for trying to illuminate each level the first time through, which means not just having all the same-color blocks touch, but also covering all the runes). It's hard to say whether that was how the game was intented to be or if there were just certain types of puzzles that I found more difficult than others. Either way, the game kept me entertained and itching to try and complete a much as I could.

I completed the game 100% in about 32 hours. The ambiant music was lovely to listen to, as it wasn't obnoxious or abrasive. However, I found that I was eventually becoming tired of the repetitive music after playing for hours and hours at a time. There are options to turn off the music and sound effects, so I ended up listening to my own music past that point. Other than those two options there is only a button to change the game from windowed mode to fullscreen. These few options work just fine for this game because there isn't really anything else that needs to be messed with. The game also has the original Blockwick "Basics," which offers even more puzzles. I felt that "Basics" was much easier so I often switched and worked on some of those puzzles when I was stuck on a more difficult one in the other section.

TL;DR Blockwick 2 is a challenging but enjoyable puzzle game with nice visuals and music that is definitely a great purchase for those interested in logical/spatial puzzle games! With both Blockwick "Basics" and Blockwick 2 in this game, there are 320+ puzzles!

Blockwick 2 is a unity-based, candy-coloured block sliding puzzle game.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
- Vibrant colors and a crisp presentation
- Mixes it up by adding block behaviours, like sticky blocks, sleeping blocks, and snake blocks
- Allows you to skip challenging levels via a mini-game, finding a pearl buried in each level
- Want more challenge? Try beating the levels by matching the symbols on the blocks to their grid locations. Adds another layer of difficulty, and is completely optional
- Has a beginner series of puzzles that was added later, giving you even more for your money

[h1]Cons[/h1]
- For some, the music may be distracting. Luckily there is a mute button.
- The difficulty didn't progress smoothly. There were some dastardly puzzles in between otherwise simple ones. Not sure if this was by design.
- The tutorial is very sparse. In specific, I found that the sticky blocks had a behaviour that I only discovered by accident. It would have been nice to explain these better to avoid getting stuck (pun intended)
- Undo only goes back one step. I was forced to reset in some sleeping block stages, where it is quite possible to become trapped.

If you enjoy casual puzzle games, Blockwick 2 is a good deal. But if sliding block puzzles aren't your thing, you probably won't be won over by Blockwick 2. I found this to be an excellent way to take a break in between tasks by leaving it running in the background and solving a puzzle here and there. Walking away and coming back to it got me past some of the more challenging levels. It's also why my playtime is so exaggerated, pay it no mind.

I strongly advise picking this up on sale. As much as I support the hard work put into Blockwick, I can't say it's worth the full sticker price.

Achievement hunters: Assuming no use of a guide, may provide a fair challenge when trying to illuminate all levels. But nothing that time and persistence won't overcome. 100% is achievable.

I never played the (mobile only?) original, so the title and developer were unfamiliar to me, and I don't know exactly which features were already present in that first entry.

The premise is fairly simple: join like-colored blocks together in contiguous groups (white blocks are the neutral exception).

This game does something that many puzzle games (at least on Steam) often overlook: offering several different puzzle gimmicks, easing you into them, and giving you lots of different use cases for each one without getting repetitive. Each specialty block concept has a set of 16 stages dedicated to exploring how that block can function. Once you've mastered a specialty block, that block type might make an appearance in a later zone, so you'll get to see how it interacts with (or obstructs) your current block type.

Some stages feature huge blocks that are difficult to maneuver; others are claustrophic - loaded up with so many blocks that there's very little room to move; others are partitioned into multiple rooms that don't connect but must function together.

Puzzles are unlocked in sequence, but the devs have mercifully included, in every level, a hidden pearl that will allow you to skip to the next puzzle if you get stuck (though even if you don't get stuck, you might want to seek them out anyway). A puzzle is considered "solved" once all the colors are grouped, but each puzzle also has a "true" solution which requires solving the puzzle while all 3 of the floor's glyph spaces are occupied by a colored block. This is a nice added challenge for the compulsive completionists.

The "Basics" level pack has also been added in, bringing an additional 144 puzzles. Basics puzzles are less complex and don't make use of all the specialty block types (which is fine!), but they do have glyphs and pearls.

The visual style is clean and bright. The art isn't cluttered, so you're able to keep your focus on the blocks. The backgrounds are just slightly tinted, and you can differentiate between the white blocks and the "island" walls. The music is pleasant and ambient but not boring. There's  also a surprising number of tracks for this type of game.

Note: I don't know if this game (as of this writing) will be accessible to colorblind players. I haven't seen any colorblindness options in the menu, and differentiating color is an absolutely integral part of every puzzle. Many of the colors appear to be roughly similar in value, so they might not be very distinguishable in greyscale.

Illumination out of ten.

Blockwick 2 is a logic game made by (yet unknown) indie studio Kieffer Bros. 

Gameplay revolves around moving differently colored blocks that, in the end, should end up connected to all blocks of the same color. Although it's already offering a good challenge on the basic principle, there are more optional objectives for those who seek bigger challenge - there is a hidden pearl in every level, that can grant you a hint in any level, and there are special marked places on the level, on which you have you connect the colored blocks if you want to feel really proud of yourself. (You can connect them anyway on the level and feel proud too, you won't just "illuminate" the level.)

Developers made a definitely great work on level design and overall game design, it feels really polished, and both relaxing and stressful, depending on your patience with harder levels and illumination. There are hundreds of levels, so don't be afraid this would be just a fun for few hours, especially if you'll want to illuminate all the levels - expect tens hours of gameplay!

Blockwick 2 is definitely a sweet puzzle game with a low price tag. There's nothing that would keep me from recommending this game, so... buy it, it's worth it!
